I read the test and the handler implementation. In the test, `command_token` is set to `"/Start@WrongBot"`, the message text becomes `"/Start@WrongBot alpha beta gamma"`, and `message.set_bot(_DummyBot("qa_bot"))` sets the bot username to `"qa_bot"`.

In `CommandHandler.check_update`, once the message passes the earlier guards, it computes:
- `command = message.text[1 : message.entities[0].length]`, which strips the leading `/` and uses the command entity length. Since the entity length is `len(command_token)`, `command` becomes `"Start@WrongBot"`.
- `command_parts = command.split("@")`, so `command_parts` becomes `["Start", "WrongBot"]`.
- `command_parts.append(message.get_bot().username)`, appending `"qa_bot"` to make sure index 1 exists even if no `@botname` was present. Here index 1 is still the original `"WrongBot"`.

Therefore at the condition on lines 196–197:
- `command_parts[1].lower()` is `"wrongbot"`
- `message.get_bot().username.lower()` is `"qa_bot"`
